newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-LAW-MAKING BODY TO CONSIDER VIDEO EXPERIMENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAW-MAKING BODY TO CONSIDER VIDEO EXPERIMENT.

text.p: A controversial proposal to experiment with video replays to help referees will be considered next month by the International Football Association Board, FIFA said on Friday.
The board, which is concerned solely with the laws of the game, is a separate entity from FIFA.
FIFA denied a report earlier on Friday that it had approved the plan and said it was totally opposed to the use of video replays in refereeing.
FIFA confirmed that the French Football Federation had asked to be allowed to experiment with video replays as a refereeing aid during a friendly match with Sweden in Paris in April.

But FIFA press chief Keith Cooper said the matter had been referred by FIFA to the International Football Board, which will meet in Belfast on March 1 to consider the issue among other proposed chances in the soccer laws.
"There is no change in the established procedure of all matters relating to the laws of the game being decided exclusively by the International Football Association Board," Cooper told Reuters.
"This request from the French Football Association clearly involves the laws of the game. Therefore, only the International Football Association Board can decide on it.
"FIFA has therefore in no way diverted from its normal policy.
"During its meeting earlier this week, which was purely consultative in nature, the FIFA referees' committee repeated its strong opposition to the use of videos in refereeing."
The French move would allow the referee to consult a television monitor at the side of the pitch to help him determine questionable incidents during play.
